summary.en-US: Vertical tabs in the sidebar: search, pin, group, snooze and back up your tabs. Local-first, no tracking, free and open source.

description.en-US:
Vertically Challenged shows all your tabs in a fast, searchable vertical list in Firefox's sidebar (or its own window).

- **Every tab in every window**, with window names. Private windows stay separate.
- **Fuzzy search** over tabs, bookmarks, history and saved sessions. Type > to run commands from the keyboard.
- **Organize your way:** Staples (a grid of the pages you use all day), pinned folders, child tabs and Firefox's own tab groups.
- **Sessions and snooze:** save sessions and window setups, restore them later, or snooze a tab until tomorrow.
- **Tab suspending:** put idle tabs to sleep to save memory.
- **Make it yours:** themes, density and layout you control, including custom CSS.
- **Full backups** with optional encryption, saved to Downloads, Nextcloud/WebDAV, S3-compatible storage or Dropbox, on a schedule you choose.
- **Free and open source** (GPLv3). No account, no analytics, no ads.

> **Firefox support is new.** It has had much less testing than the Chrome version, so there will be rough edges. Keep backups of anything you cannot afford to lose.

Found a problem or have a fix? [Open an issue or send a pull request on GitHub](https://github.com/humdedum1/vertically-challenged).

version.approval_notes: The source is attached as a ZIP and also at https://github.com/humdedum1/vertically-challenged. Build: Node.js 22, then `npm ci && npm run build:firefox`; the output in .output/firefox-mv3 is what was submitted. The JavaScript is minified by Vite (WXT). A build transform in wxt.config.ts replaces two innerHTML assignments in Svelte's runtime with DOMParser. Details: docs/store/AMO.md.
